name: Shyama Prasad Mukherjee
role: Indian politician: Hindu Mahasabha leader, Union minister for industry and supply (1947-1950), founder-president of the Bharatiya Jana Sangh (1901-1953)
summary: Mukherjee, a Hindu nationalist politician, opposed Article 370 and demanded Kashmir's full integration, opposed the Hindu Code Bill as destroying Hindu custom, accepted Hindi as the national language while defending regional languages, wanted a non-aligned India, and wrote that Hindus should build a Hindu nation.

sources.title: Eminent Parliamentarians Monograph Series: Dr. Syama Prasad Mookerjee (Lok Sabha Secretariat, New Delhi, 1990), with excerpts from his speeches in the Constituent Assembly, Provisional Parliament and Lok Sabha, Internet Archive full text (his speech excerpts only; the profile is the editors')
sources.author: Syama Prasad Mookerjee (speeches); Lok Sabha Secretariat (compilation)
sources.usedFor: Speeches on Article 370 and Kashmir, the Hindu Code Bill, Hindi and regional languages, linguistic provinces, preventive detention, foreign policy and the Nehru-Liaquat pact.

sources.title: Leaves from a Diary (autobiographical writings 1939-1946, ed. Ashutosh Mukherjee et al.), Internet Archive full text
sources.author: Syama Prasad Mookerjee
sources.usedFor: His reflections on Bengal under the Home Department, the Hindu Mahasabha and Partition.

notes: First audit. Read by theme the Lok Sabha Secretariat's 1990 monograph (his Constituent Assembly, Provisional Parliament and Lok Sabha speeches: Article 370, the Hindu Code Bill, Hindi and regional languages, linguistic provinces, preventive detention, foreign policy, the Nehru-Liaquat pact) and his 'Leaves from a Diary'. On preventive detention he spoke from both sides (recalling Rowlatt, accepting restrictive measures against hostile elements), so no answer was drawn. His acts as Industry minister (the Industrial Policy Resolution of 1948 and his 1950 resignation over the Nehru-Liaquat pact) are described in his speeches but were not opened as records. Most statements stay null.
